question: Which issues are growing fastest, and are any of them new?

answer.answer_markdown:
**Almost nothing is growing, and nothing is new.** Growth can only be answered from the written-complaint corpus of 4,425 contacts, which spans two years; the recorded conversations cover a single month and give no baseline at all. Running the emerging screen on the complaints at the latest week tested 9 themes and flagged 1 - promised callback or follow-up communication never occurs - on 6 contacts in the last three weeks against 1.78 expected, z 2.79.

That flag does not survive a second look. The same theme is not robust over an eight-week window, and across the full two years its monthly share is flat, down 1.1 share points. It is a short burst on a small base, not a trend. Treat it as something to watch next month rather than something to staff for now.

The one theme with a genuine upward trend is a close cousin of it: promised credit, refund, or bonus not applied, 56 contacts, rising by 1.3 share points with a t-statistic of 2.74. The third mover, check deposit hold extended without justification, is flat at 0.1 points, t 0.84. At the coarser level of contact reasons nothing is rising at all; the only reason moving is fees and charges, 287 contacts, and it is falling, t-statistic -2.11. So the honest headline is a stable complaint mix with one broken-promise theme inching up.

On newness, the answer is a clean no. The screen restricted to genuinely new themes returns nothing above the threshold. The flagged callback theme was first seen nearly two years before the as-of week, so it is long-standing rather than emerging. The newest-looking candidate among the top movers, check deposit hold extended without justification, first appeared late last year on 22 contacts - too thin to pass the threshold, and worth a second look only if it keeps accumulating.

claims.statement: At the latest week the emerging screen on the complaints tested 9 themes and flagged exactly 1 - promised callback or follow-up communication never occurs - on 6 recent contacts against 1.78 expected, z 2.79, and it is not robust over an eight-week window.
No theme qualifies as new: the new-themes-only screen returns nothing above the threshold, and the single flagged theme was first seen nearly two years before the as-of week.

Of the three fastest-moving complaint themes, only promised credit, refund, or bonus not applied is genuinely rising (56 contacts, up 1.3 share points, t 2.74); the flagged callback theme is flat at -1.1 points and check deposit holds are flat at 0.1 points, t 0.84.

caveats: Every growth number here is scoped to the complaints corpus: 4,425 real written complaints about one bank, July 2024 to June 2026. The index also holds 1,000 synthetic agent/customer phone conversations from September 2023 alone, which have no prior period to compare against and are therefore excluded from all trend and emergence claims.

The single emerging flag rests on 6 contacts in three weeks. With 9 themes tested the screen expects about 0.05 false positives, but the theme fails the eight-week robustness check, so the burst may simply be noise.

Written complaints are a self-selected channel. A rise in a theme can reflect changes in complaint-filing behaviour or in the regulator's intake rather than a change in the underlying customer experience.
Contact reason direction is a within-window trend: the corpus has no earlier equal period to compare against, so 'previous period' counts read as zero rather than as a real decline.
followups: Promised credit or refund not applied and promised callback never happens are both broken-promise themes - if they are merged and tracked as one, is the combined trend rising strongly enough to act on?
Does check deposit hold extended without justification keep accumulating over the next two months, or does it stall at the level where it is still too thin to flag?
